questions.q: Why won't simply adding more replicas or deleting the overloaded pods fix this incident?
options: Because Kubernetes doesn't allow deleting pods during an incident
Because neither action touches the root cause — with no spread rule, the scheduler can just as easily recreate the same zone imbalance
Because adding replicas always costs more than Driftwood's budget allows
Because deleting pods is a prohibited operation in AKS
questions.explain: Without a topology spread constraint, kube-scheduler has no new information and can rebuild the exact same imbalance, possibly after a brief outage from the deletion itself.

questions.q: In the topologySpreadConstraints block Theo adds, what does maxSkew: 1 guarantee?
options: Exactly one pod will run in each zone, no matter how many replicas exist
The pod count in the most-loaded zone can differ from the least-loaded zone by at most 1
Only one zone is allowed to run checkout-api pods at all
The Deployment can only have 1 replica total
questions.explain: maxSkew: 1 bounds the difference in matching-pod count between the most- and least-loaded topology domain to at most one pod.

Ignores the spread constraint and schedules the pod anyway
questions.explain: DoNotSchedule means the scheduler will leave the pod unscheduled (Pending) rather than break the configured spread.

questions.q: Why does Theo confirm the PodDisruptionBudget is in place before applying the fix?
options: The PDB is unrelated and doesn't need to be checked
Because the rolling update that applies this Pod-template change needs the PDB's minimum-available guarantee so fixing an availability problem doesn't cause a worse one mid-sale
Because PDBs control the dollar cost of the cluster
Because PDBs determine which availability zone pods are scheduled into
questions.explain: kubectl apply on a changed Pod template triggers a rolling update; the PDB (set during Lesson 8's load-testing work) guarantees a minimum number of checkout-api pods stay available throughout that rollout.

questions.q: What does labelSelector.matchLabels.app: checkout-api do inside the topologySpreadConstraints block?
options: It deletes any pod that isn't labeled checkout-api
It restricts the skew calculation to only count other checkout-api pods, not every pod in the cluster
It sets the container image for checkout-api
It defines the Kubernetes namespace
questions.explain: The labelSelector scopes the spread calculation to pods matching app: checkout-api, so unrelated workloads elsewhere in the cluster don't affect the skew math.
